# Settle 049e's one documentary claim with a live measurement

## Context

Bug `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` made the DC comment ceiling configurable
(`[tool.rebar.reconciler].comment_max_chars`, default 32767) and DROPPED the idea of
auto-discovering the ceiling from `/rest/api/2/application-properties`, on the grounds that the
`/advanced-settings` sub-resource where `jira.text.field.character.limit` is actually exposed
requires the global "Administer Jira" permission, while rebar authenticates as an ordinary user's PAT.

**That conclusion is DOCUMENTARY, not measured.** 049e's agent tried to probe live and could not: the
`tests/external/live_jira_dc` harness image is linux/amd64 only and its README records three measured
attempts where Jira never became usable within an hour on the arm64 workstation. So no 403 was ever
captured. 049e's AC asked for an EMPIRICAL determination and got a documentary one; rather than tick
that box on inference, the limitation was recorded and the probe deferred here.

## Why this is worth doing rather than dropping

The probe is genuinely runnable — just not on that host. The `jira-dc-harness` job in
`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` runs the same harness on GitHub Actions' amd64 runners,
where the image works. So this is a deferred measurement, not an impossible one.

## What it does NOT change

049e's remedy stands either way. Configuration is the correct fix whether or not the endpoint is
readable: a readable endpoint would enable an OPTIONAL auto-discovery convenience on top of the config
key, not invalidate it. So this ticket cannot regress 049e — it can only add an enhancement or confirm
the drop. That independence is why 049e was closeable with this leg outstanding.

## Approach

Add a single cell to the live DC suite that requests `/rest/api/2/application-properties` (and the
`/advanced-settings` sub-resource) with the harness's ordinary non-admin PAT and RECORDS the outcome —
status code and body shape — asserting only that the outcome is one of the two documented
possibilities, so the cell reports a fact rather than pinning a guess.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a live DC cell requests `/rest/api/2/application-properties` with a NON-ADMIN PAT and records
      the observed status code, run id, and job name on this ticket
- [x] the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource is probed separately, because that is where
      `jira.text.field.character.limit` is exposed and its permission requirement may differ
- [x] the cell distinguishes 403 (permission, the documented expectation) from 404 (endpoint absent on
      8.17.1) from 200 (readable) — a bare non-200 assertion does NOT satisfy this
- [x] the outcome is written back onto `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` so its documentary claim is either
      confirmed or corrected in the record
- [x] if the endpoint IS readable, a follow-up is filed for optional auto-discovery; 049e's config key
      remains the supported mechanism either way

## Measured and closed (run 30944241768) — see MEASURED-275E-A

    GET /rest/api/2/application-properties                    non-admin PAT: 403 | admin: 200 (72)
    GET /rest/api/2/application-properties/advanced-settings  non-admin PAT: 403 | admin: 200 (33)

Both paths are PRESENT but PRIVILEGED. The admin leg in the same run is what distinguishes that from
"absent on 8.17.1"; three controls (the PAT authenticates as the new user, that user lacks ADMINISTER,
and the admin comparison) are asserted rather than assumed, which is what the "no bare non-200" criterion
required.

049e's documentary claim is CONFIRMED and its remedy stands: `comment_max_chars` remains the mechanism.
The final criterion's conditional does not fire — the endpoint is NOT readable by rebar's PAT, so no
auto-discovery follow-up is filed.
